title: How small is small
subtitle: The kernel, every brick and the hero budget, in bytes.
lead: "Tiny" means nothing without a number. Fizlet's kernel is 3,413 bytes gzip on 0.21.0, against a budget of 4,096 that fails the build when crossed. Every brick has its own budget, a page hero has one too, and the site shows only numbers the build measured. Here is each number, and how we get it.

items.label: the page build: kernel + slot + input + fx (budget 7,168 B)
a hero's live chunk: kernel, bricks and the scene's own code
`fizlet.js`: one script tag, every brick but debug

body.text: One function measures everything: `scripts/sizes.mjs`. It bundles each entry with esbuild (ESM, ES2022, minified), gzips the result and compares it with the entry's budget. 1 KB is 1,024 bytes. A brick's number includes every part of the kernel it imports, so it is what a page pays for that brick alone.

`npm run size` runs it in CI and fails over budget. The website calls the same function while it builds, so the numbers on the [budgets page](/docs/budgets/) and on every brick page are the ones CI checked, never typed. The site test measures again and fails if a page disagrees.

items: **0.1.0: about 2.6 KB.** The shared clock, the fixed step, auto-pause, pools, the event ring, the seeded random and the ledger.
**0.3.5: 2,839 → 3,106 B.** Hardening: options checked at setup, a throwing hook stops only its own engine, `destroy()` idempotent.
**0.5.0: 3,106 → 3,275 B.** The page profile: `settle` (no frames once nothing moves) and the `fps` cap.
**0.7.0: 3,275 → 3,347 B.** `engine.timing` and `engine.live`: typed-array slots, so reading them never boxes a number.
**0.19.0: 3,439 B (+17 B).** The fps cap now caps `requestAnimationFrame` itself: a capped hero asks for 30 frames a second instead of one per vsync.
**0.21.0: 3,413 B.** Headroom, no behaviour change: the ledger's private fields got one-letter names, and its host-changed style check and put-back became shared helpers.

body.text: Each step bought something you can test. That is the rule for a budget: it moves only with a reason, and the changelog says how much.

items.title: steer 1,156 B · sound 1,019 B
items.body: Movers on typed arrays with seek, flee, arrive, wander and patrol; a synth with nine cues and no audio files.

items.title: coach 1,220 B · input 1,335 B · collide 1,265 B
items.body: Tutorial steps and tips; keys, pointer and a touch stick as intents; a fixed-capacity spatial hash.

items.title: rules 1,318 B · hud 1,325 B · camera 1,475 B · sprite 1,437 B
items.body: Waves, drops and score; change-only readouts; pan and zoom of a DOM stage; pixel characters as data.

items.title: grid 1,603 B · presence 1,834 B · slot 1,819 B
items.body: A board with A* paths and sight; lockstep input exchange; a lazy scene for an Astro slot.

items.title: perf 2,042 B · pad 2,074 B · embed 2,016 B · timeline 2,120 B
items.body: The players' perf overlay; touch controls; a drop-in game toggle; keyframes on the kernel clock.

items.title: match 2,652 B · fx 2,797 B · ui 2,893 B + 4,974 B css · board-page 4,136 B
items.body: Match flow; pooled particles and the blast; the Board UI keys; the host page as the board.

body.text: A landing-page hero's live chunk (kernel, bricks and the scene's own code) has a budget of 10 KB gzip. The page build takes 7,128 B of it, which leaves about 3 KB for the scene. A test fails if sound, debug, the pad, the HUD, match or the Board UI get into the page build.

The two story heroes on the home page fit: the layers scene's live chunk is 9,700 B and the fizz scene's 8,723 B. Neither loads until its slot nears the viewport, and both settle to zero frames once nothing moves.

blocks.heading: When a budget had to move

body.text: **`fizlet/timeline` missed its target.** We aimed for 1,536 B. Keyframes, easing tables, stagger, labels, repeat and yoyo, controls and revert came to 2,050 B when it shipped in 0.19.0, so its budget is 2,304 B, and the changelog says so. On 0.21.0 it is 2,120 B.

**`fizlet/board-page` moves when the kernel does.** It bundles only the kernel's phase constants, but esbuild's renamer counts the whole engine module, so any kernel edit moves it by about 2 bytes. In 0.19.0 it sat at 4,095 of 4,096, so the budget went to 4,128 rather than chase renames; it is 4,193 now that its hit test uses steer's exact `hypot`, and on 0.21.0 it is 4,136 B.

items.q: Why gzip and not minified bytes?
items.a: Gzip is what crosses the wire for a script on almost every host, so it is what a visitor pays. Where a change is about minified bytes, the changelog gives them too.

It is a shell, not a brick: it composes the kernel, board-page, input, the pad, sound, the HUD and the Board UI keys, so a page arcade game is only its rules and art. A card game that leaves out the skirmish HUD ships 18,295 B of it.

items.q: Do you compare with other engines?
items.a: No. We publish what we measured on our own code, with how we measured it.
